Annotated data matrix

Source: R/anndata.R
AnnData.Rd

AnnData() creates an annotated data matrix of n_obs observations by n_vars variables, following Python anndata 0.13.4. It wraps the AnnData R6 class (ADR 0002), so objects have reference semantics: b <- a aliases and does not copy.

Usage

AnnData(
  X = NULL,
  obs = NULL,
  var = NULL,
  uns = NULL,
  ...,
  obsm = NULL,
  varm = NULL,
  layers = NULL,
  raw = NULL,
  shape = NULL,
  obsp = NULL,
  varp = NULL,
  filename = NULL,
  filemode = NULL
)

Arguments

X

A numeric or logical matrix, or a Matrix sparse matrix, or NULL. An AnnData supplies all its Slots, and then obs, var, uns, obsm, varm, obsp and varp must not be given. A data.frame or DataFrame is converted to a matrix, with a warning when its columns differ in type, and its row and column names become the obs_names and var_names. Automatic row names are ignored.

obs, var

Annotations of observations and variables as NULL, a named list, a data.frame or a DataFrame. When X is a frame with names, these must match them, unless they have no names of their own.

uns

Unstructured annotation, a named list or NULL.

...

Must be empty, so that the arguments after uns are named.

obsm, varm, obsp, varp, layers

Aligned mappings as named lists or NULL. An NA name in layers addresses X.

raw

An AnnData or a named list with the elements X, var and varm, whose contents become the Raw, or NULL. Without X the Raw is made from the X, var and varm of the new object.

shape

Integer vector c(n_obs, n_vars) used when X is NULL.

filename, filemode

Backed mode (not yet supported).

Value

An AnnData object.

Details

X is stored in the layers storage under the NA key (ADR 0004) and adata$X aliases it. The shape comes from X, from shape or is inferred from obs and var. Giving both shape and X is an error. Without names, observations and variables are named "0", "1", ..., "n-1" as in Python.

Fields

  • X: the data matrix, or NULL

  • uns: unstructured annotation, a named list

  • obs, var: annotation S4Vectors::DataFrames

  • obs_names, var_names: character names

  • n_obs, n_vars, shape: dimensions

  • is_view: whether the object is a View made by adata[i, j]

  • isbacked, filename and file: whether the object is backed by a file (read_h5ad(backed = )), the path of that file or NULL, and the file manager (file$open(), file$close(), file$is_open)

The dimension and backing fields are read-only and assigning to them raises an anndata_read_only_error.

Backed mode

read_h5ad(file, backed = "r") (or "r+") keeps X and raw$X on disk and reads every other Slot into memory. print() shows backed at '<file>'. adata$file$close() closes the file but keeps the object backed, and the next read of X opens it again. The file is closed when the object is garbage collected.

Views

adata[i, j] returns a View that shares data with adata, as in Python. X, layers, obsm, varm, obsp and varp are read from the parent on every access, so a View shows later changes to the parent's X. obs, var, uns and raw are snapshots taken when the View is created. A View of a View refers to the original parent. Modifying a View turns it into an independent object (is_view becomes FALSE) and leaves the parent unchanged. This includes nested forms such as view$X[1, 1] <- 0, view$obs$col <- x and view$uns$k <- v, and deleting a key with view$obsm[["k"]] <- NULL. Where Python warns, an anndata_implicit_modification_warning is raised. R cannot tell view$obs$col <- x from view$obs <- x, so both warn with the message for assigning the whole Slot. copy() of a View returns an independent object, transpose() raises an error, and writing a View to h5ad or zarr writes the subset.

Deviations from Python

Accessors return plain R values and not View wrappers. In Python x = view.X; x[0, 0] = 1 modifies the View, but in R x <- view$X; x[1, 1] <- 1 only changes x and the View is unaffected. Assign through the View (view$X[1, 1] <- 1) to modify it. For a View of a backed object this makes the View independent with a warning, where Python silently changes nothing. See vignette("deviations") for the full list.

Deprecated methods

Python 0.13.4 deprecates these methods, so they warn on every call with the classes anndata_deprecated_warning and anndata_future_warning: obs_keys(), var_keys(), obsm_keys(), varm_keys(), uns_keys(), obs_vector() and var_vector().

Examples

adata <- AnnData(matrix(as.numeric(1:6), nrow = 3))
adata$shape
#> [1] 3 2
adata$obs_names
#> [1] "0" "1" "2"

# From a data frame, whose names are kept
df <- data.frame(a = c(1, 2), b = c(3, 4), row.names = c("r1", "r2"))
AnnData(df)$obs_names
#> [1] "r1" "r2"

# From another AnnData
AnnData(adata)$shape
#> [1] 3 2
